messages:
olivia (Support): @jia thanks for the report — we want to grab a trace so eng can correlate. Can you send any request IDs or debug tokens you see? Best things: response headers (X-Request-ID / request-id), SDK debug token, or a HAR/curl that reproduces the failing call.

jia (Customer): I tried looking but can't find any request-id in our app responses. We go through an internal proxy.

olivia (Support): OK — proxies commonly strip custom headers. Two quick asks: 1) run a curl from your laptop hitting the same endpoint (this will show response headers). 2) If mobile, take an SDK debug dump or a HAR via remote debug.

ram (Eng): Copying the curl I usually ask for (replace placeholders):

```bash
# show request + response headers and body
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  -D -   # prints response headers
```

If the proxy strips X-Request-ID, the response headers printed by `-D -` will still show any other correlators. Also try `-v` which prints the request/response exchange.

ram (Eng): If you can only reproduce via the app, please capture a HAR from Chrome (or from remote device via Chrome remote debug for Android). Steps: DevTools -> Network -> right click -> Save all as HAR with content. Attach the HAR file; we can extract request/response headers and bodies.

jia (Customer): We can get HAR from web flow. For Android native flow — how to get the SDK debug?

ram (Eng): For Android native: enable verbose SDK logs and run `adb logcat | grep -i redwood` (or the package name). Look for lines including `session_ref`, `debug_token`, or `request_id`. Example snippet we look for: 

```
2026-03-15 12:34:56.789 D/RedwoodSDK: send request id=abc123 span=0x4f2 session_ref=sr-7f9 debug_token=dt:xyz
```

If you can't see those, capture a short log file and paste the relevant lines (no PII). For iOS, share the Xcode device logs.

olivia (Support): A couple extra tips:
- If you only have a proxy trace, look for any header named `x-request-id`, `request-id`, `x-correlation-id`, or cloud trace headers like `x-amzn-trace-id` / `traceparent`.
- On server-side proxies, sometimes the original header is renamed to `x-forwarded-request-id`; include anything that looks like an ID.

eng-bot: Escalation ticket created: ESC-8921. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/escalations/ESC-8921 (automated).

ram (Eng): If you can grab a minimal curl output, please paste the exact `-D -` response headers block and the matching request headers (from `-v`) here. Example to paste: the whole header block including `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` and the following headers so we can match server-side logs.

jia (Customer): Got it — I'll send a HAR from the web repro and run the curl. Will paste the header block here shortly.

olivia (Support): thanks — when you upload, please mark the HAR file with the timestamp and include the curl output + a note if the call went through a proxy/CDN. That saves a round-trip. :thumbsup:

ram (Eng): One more fallback: if nothing shows, we can ask you to turn on a short period of SDK debug-level traces in prod for a specific user session and then share the `session_ref` we ask you to create from the Console (Console -> Sessions -> Create debug bundle). That bundle includes the trace we need.

jia (Customer): Uploaded HAR (har-file-2026-03-15.har) and curl headers pasted in the ticket. Thanks, will wait for next steps.

olivia (Support): Received — we'll take a look and update ESC-8921. If we need the SDK log we'll ping with the exact session_ref to collect.

ram (Eng): Thanks — quick note for future repros: adding `-H "X-Debug: 1"` to the request sometimes forces the proxy to echo back internal IDs; worth trying if your proxy supports debug headers.
